_about: Mars overlay: replaces the Moon's milestone list (arrays replace). Ids are prefixed or distinct from the Moon's, because records are kept per campaign. Rules in rules/milestones.ts; zone sizes and the sunset band in data/mars/tuning.json milestones. Facts fact-checked November 15, 2026 (M5). Mars step 4b adds the twenty new milestones of the Mars sites plan (game-design.md, New Mars milestones; triggers provisional, for Chieri's review): 28 in all. Their trigger rules come in Mars step 5a, so until then some never fire (photo crater-wall and dustdevil, record with seconds, transects with zones or no zone, the delta-foot zone); none fires wrongly. howTo lines (new milestones only) hold no numbers: ui/milestoneText.ts milestoneHowTo fills them.
_interface: money and rp are placeholders set with Owner A. Sized so a run that drives, photographs or drills earns several times what a rover idling at the lander earns (Touchdown, perhaps Storm survivor).
_rewards: Money and RP of the twenty new milestones are the decided starting values (game-design.md, New Mars milestones); the Mars balance step (7) tunes them. Clean run pays no money until then (decided in Phase 0: no money for what an idle rover earns). Blue sunset 70 -> 100 (decided November 15).

milestones.name: Touchdown
milestones.summary: The rover has landed on the floor of Jezero crater and deployed from the lander.
milestones.fact: The Soviet Mars 3 lander made the first soft landing on Mars on December 2, 1971, but stopped transmitting within seconds; NASA's Viking 1 made the first lasting, successful landing on July 20, 1976.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "NASA Mars Orbiter Images May Show 1971 Soviet Lander" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasa-mars-orbiter-images-may-show-1971-soviet-lander/); NASA Science, "Viking 1" (science.nasa.gov/mission/viking-1/)

milestones.name: Odometer
milestones.summary: Total distance driven: {meters} m.
milestones.fact: Opportunity drove 45.16 km on Mars between 2004 and 2018, a record for another world until Perseverance passed it in October 2026.
milestones.source: NASA Science, "NASA's Perseverance Sets Off-World Record for Total Distance Driven" (science.nasa.gov/blogs/perseverance-mars-rover/2026/10/12/nasas-perseverance-sets-off-world-record-for-total-distance-driven/)

milestones.name: Mapper
milestones.summary: The rover has surveyed {share}% of the map.
milestones.fact: During its 2021 landing, Perseverance's Terrain-Relative Navigation matched descent-camera images to an onboard map made from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter images, then steered toward a safe spot in Jezero.
milestones.source: USGS, "Mars 2020 Mission to be Guided by USGS Astrogeology Maps" (usgs.gov/news/mars-2020-mission-be-guided-usgs-astrogeology-maps)

milestones.name: Night drive
milestones.summary: Distance driven after dark, by the rover's own lights: {meters} m.
milestones.fact: Martian nights are brutally cold: on its 43rd and 44th sols (April 2021), Perseverance's weather station recorded a low of -83 °C at Jezero, so the rover keeps its electronics warm with heat from its nuclear power source and electric heaters.
milestones.source: NASA, "NASA's First Weather Report from Jezero Crater on Mars" (nasa.gov/feature/nasa-s-first-weather-report-from-jezero-crater-on-mars); NASA JPL, Mars 2020 press kit, "Power" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/press_kits/mars_2020/launch/mission/spacecraft/power/)

milestones.name: Storm survivor
milestones.summary: The dust storm has cleared and the rover is still operating.
milestones.fact: A 2018 planet-wide dust storm blocked sunlight to Opportunity, which last contacted Earth on June 10; NASA ended its mission on February 13, 2019. Nuclear-powered Curiosity kept working.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "NASA's Opportunity Rover Mission on Mars Comes to End" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-opportunity-rover-mission-on-mars-comes-to-end/)

milestones.name: Sand crossing
milestones.summary: The rover crossed Séítah's sand ripples without getting stuck.
milestones.howTo: Drive across Séítah's sand ripples without getting stuck.
milestones.fact: In 2009 NASA's Spirit rover got stuck in soft sand at a spot called Troy; after months of attempts to free it, NASA made it a stationary research platform in January 2010.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "NASA's Mars Rover Spirit Starts a New Chapter" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-mars-rover-spirit-starts-a-new-chapter), January 26, 2010

milestones.name: Clean run
milestones.summary: The rover finished all ten sols without damage.
milestones.howTo: Finish all {days} sols without damage.
milestones.fact: Opportunity was designed for a 90-sol mission on Mars and kept working for more than 14 years, until a planet-wide dust storm in 2018.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "NASA's Opportunity Rover Mission on Mars Comes to End" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-opportunity-rover-mission-on-mars-comes-to-end/)

milestones.name: Delta layers
milestones.summary: The camera imaged the layered front of Jezero's ancient river delta.
milestones.fact: Perseverance's 2021 images of the 'Kodiak' butte showed delta layers laid down by a river flowing into a lake, confirming that Jezero once held a lake.
milestones.source: Mangold et al., Science 374 (2021), "Perseverance rover reveals an ancient delta-lake system and flood deposits at Jezero crater, Mars" (doi.org/10.1126/science.abl4051)

milestones.name: Core sample
milestones.summary: The drill collected a rock core, away from the ground the lander disturbed.
milestones.fact: Perseverance's first coring attempt on Jezero's crater floor, in August 2021, came back empty: the rock was too crumbly to hold together as a core, so the rover drove on and tried again.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "NASA's Perseverance Team Assessing First Mars Sampling Attempt" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-perseverance-team-assessing-first-mars-sampling-attempt/)

milestones.name: Blue sunset
milestones.summary: The camera photographed the Sun setting over Jezero crater.
milestones.fact: Curiosity photographed a blue sunset in Gale crater on April 15, 2015 (sol 956): fine dust in Mars' air lets blue light pass through more efficiently, so blue stays closer to the Sun.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "Sunset in Mars' Gale Crater" (science.nasa.gov/photojournal/sunset-in-mars-gale-crater)

milestones.name: Crater wall
milestones.summary: The camera imaged the far inner wall of a young crater, a natural cross-section through the crater floor.
milestones.howTo: Photograph a young crater's far inner wall from its rim, with the crater's center in the frame.
milestones.fact: Crater walls are natural cross-sections: Opportunity spent about two years at Victoria crater, whose layered walls preserve ancient wind-blown dunes.
milestones.source: Squyres et al., Science 324 (2009), "Exploration of Victoria Crater by the Mars Rover Opportunity" (doi.org/10.1126/science.1170355)

milestones.name: Dust devil
milestones.summary: The camera caught a dust devil crossing the floor of Jezero crater.
milestones.howTo: Photograph a passing dust devil.
milestones.fact: Perseverance's weather sensors counted about four whirlwinds a sol passing over Jezero, and over a quarter of them were carrying dust.
milestones.source: Newman et al., Science Advances 8 (2022), "The dynamic atmospheric and aeolian environment of Jezero crater, Mars" (doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abn3783)

milestones.name: Séítah core
milestones.summary: The drill collected a core of Séítah's olivine-rich rock.
milestones.howTo: Drill a sample inside Séítah, at least {minDistance} m from the lander.
milestones.fact: Perseverance's PIXL showed that Séítah's rock at Brac is an olivine cumulate: olivine crystals that settled out of a thick, slowly cooling body of magma.
milestones.source: Liu et al., Science 377 (2022), "An olivine cumulate outcrop on the floor of Jezero crater, Mars" (doi.org/10.1126/science.abo2756)

milestones.name: Signs of an ancient lake
milestones.summary: The drill collected a core at the foot of the delta, from layers laid down in Jezero's ancient lake.
milestones.howTo: Drill a sample at the foot of the delta, where blocks fallen from its layers lie. Once per campaign.
milestones.fact: In July 2022 Perseverance cored 'Wildcat Ridge' at the delta front, a fine-grained rock that formed as mud and fine sand settled in the lake that once filled Jezero crater.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "NASA's Perseverance Rover Investigates Geologically Rich Mars Terrain" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-perseverance-rover-investigates-geologically-rich-mars-terrain/)

milestones.name: Rock collection
milestones.summary: The X-ray spectrometer has read another kind of Mars rock.
milestones.howTo: Read {rocks} different rock types with the X-ray spectrometer. Each site has its own rocks.
milestones.fact: Perseverance's X-ray spectrometer PIXL maps a rock's chemistry grain by grain; in Séítah it found olivine-rich rock, and carbonate and salts that water left in it.
milestones.source: Liu et al., Science 377 (2022) (doi.org/10.1126/science.abo2756); Tice et al., Science Advances 8 (2022) (doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abp9084)

milestones.name: Rare rock
milestones.summary: The X-ray spectrometer read a flood conglomerate: rounded pebbles cemented together, carried into the lake by a flood.
milestones.howTo: Find the one boulder of a rock found nowhere else and read it with the X-ray spectrometer. Once per campaign.
milestones.fact: Boulders up to about 1.5 m across in the delta's top layers show that floods once swept big rocks into Jezero's lake. This flood boulder is placed by design, inspired by them.
milestones.source: Mangold et al., Science 374 (2021), "Perseverance rover reveals an ancient delta-lake system and flood deposits at Jezero crater, Mars" (doi.org/10.1126/science.abl4051)

milestones.name: Documented sample
milestones.summary: The camera documented a boulder the X-ray spectrometer had read.
milestones.howTo: Photograph a boulder the X-ray spectrometer has read this mission, in frame, from within {range} m.
milestones.fact: WATSON, a close-up camera on Perseverance's arm, images the texture of the rock patches the rover's instruments study, down to grains a millimeter or two across.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "WATSON's View of Bellegarde" (jpl.nasa.gov/images/pia24770-watsons-view-of-bellegarde/); NASA, "WATSON's View of Dourbes in Mars' Jezero Crater" (science.nasa.gov/photojournal/watsons-view-of-dourbes-in-mars-jezero-crater)

milestones.name: Organic signals
milestones.summary: The organics spectrometer finished a reading of a boulder on the crater floor.
milestones.howTo: Finish an organics reading on a boulder more than {minDistance} m from the lander. Once at each of up to {sites} sites, each {sampleSpacing} m from the others.
milestones.fact: SHERLOC found signals consistent with organic molecules in all ten crater-floor targets it studied in Máaz and Séítah; processes without life can also make such molecules.
milestones.source: Sharma et al., Nature 619 (2023), "Diverse organic-mineral associations in Jezero crater, Mars" (doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06143-z)

milestones.name: Lake organics
milestones.summary: The organics spectrometer finished a reading of a boulder fallen from the delta's lake layers.
milestones.howTo: Finish an organics reading on a boulder at the foot of the delta.
milestones.fact: At 'Wildcat Ridge', a mudstone at the delta front, SHERLOC recorded the strongest signals consistent with organic molecules of the mission so far (2022); such molecules can also form without life.
milestones.source: NASA JPL, "NASA's Perseverance Rover Investigates Geologically Rich Mars Terrain" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-perseverance-rover-investigates-geologically-rich-mars-terrain/)

milestones.name: Remote reading
milestones.summary: The laser spectrometer read a boulder from a distance.
milestones.howTo: Read a boulder with the laser spectrometer. Once at each of up to {sites} sites, each {sampleSpacing} m from the others.
milestones.fact: SuperCam, on Perseverance's mast, fires its laser at rocks up to about 7 m away and reads the light of the tiny spark it makes.
milestones.source: CNES, SuperCam (supercam.cnes.fr)

milestones.name: Rock from afar
milestones.summary: The laser spectrometer read the layered rock of the delta cliff.
milestones.howTo: From the foot of the delta, read the delta cliff with the laser spectrometer.
milestones.fact: SuperCam's microphone records the snap of each laser shot on Mars; the sound changes with the rock the laser hits.
milestones.source: Maurice et al., Nature 605 (2022), "In situ recording of Mars soundscape" (doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-04679-0)

milestones.name: Buried layers
milestones.summary: The radar profiled the layers beneath the ground.
milestones.howTo: Switch the radar on and drive {meters} m that passes a young crater's thrown-out rock, Séítah or the delta front. Once for each place, up to {sites}.
milestones.fact: Perseverance's radar, RIMFAX, imaged rock layers beneath Jezero's floor along the rover's first 3 km, tilted by up to about 15° and seen to about 15 m deep.
milestones.source: Hamran et al., Science Advances 8 (2022), "Ground penetrating radar observations of subsurface structures in the floor of Jezero crater, Mars" (doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abp8564)

milestones.name: Long profile
milestones.summary: The radar recorded a long unbroken profile of the ground beneath the crater floor.
milestones.howTo: Switch the radar on and drive {meters} m without switching it off, more than {minDistance} m from the lander.
milestones.fact: RIMFAX sounds the ground while Perseverance drives, so its picture of the layers beneath Jezero's floor grows with every drive.
milestones.source: Hamran et al., Science Advances 8 (2022), "Ground penetrating radar observations of subsurface structures in the floor of Jezero crater, Mars" (doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abp8564)

milestones.name: Hydrated ground
milestones.summary: The neutron spectrometer located ground richer in hydrogen than anywhere else nearby.
milestones.howTo: Somewhere on the crater floor the neutron spectrometer reads higher than anywhere else. Find that ground and drive through it with the spectrometer on.
milestones.fact: Curiosity's neutron instrument DAN saw the hydrogen in the ground beneath it change from place to place along its drives in Gale crater. This hydrated ground is placed by design.
milestones.source: Litvak et al., JGR Planets 119 (2014), 1259 (doi.org/10.1002/2013JE004556)

milestones.name: Hydrogen traverse
milestones.summary: The neutron spectrometer surveyed the hydrogen in the ground along the rover's drive.
milestones.howTo: Switch the neutron spectrometer on and drive {meters} m that passes Séítah or the delta front. Once for each, up to {sites}.
milestones.fact: From orbit, Mars Odyssey's neutron spectrometer found ground holding the equivalent of 2 to 10% water in places near the equator.
milestones.source: Feldman et al., Journal of Geophysical Research 109 (2004), E09006

milestones.name: Storm log
milestones.summary: The weather mast logged the dust storm from inside it.
milestones.howTo: Keep the weather mast switched on through the dust storm, more than {minDistance} m from the lander.
milestones.fact: In January 2022 a regional dust storm passed over Perseverance; its weather station logged winds up to 20 m/s before the wind sensor was damaged, while the rover's cameras watched dust lifting around it.
milestones.source: Lemmon et al., Geophysical Research Letters 49 (2022), "Dust, Sand, and Winds Within an Active Martian Storm in Jezero Crater" (doi.org/10.1029/2022GL100126)

milestones.name: Night weather
milestones.summary: The weather mast logged the air through a Martian night.
milestones.howTo: Keep the weather mast switched on, with the rover awake, through part of a night, more than {minDistance} m from the lander.
milestones.fact: Perseverance's weather station measures the air around the clock; on sols 43 and 44 (April 2021) it logged a high of -22 °C and a low of -83 °C at Jezero.
milestones.source: NASA, "NASA's First Weather Report from Jezero Crater on Mars" (nasa.gov/feature/nasa-s-first-weather-report-from-jezero-crater-on-mars)

milestones.name: Dust devil pass
milestones.summary: The weather mast recorded a dust devil passing the rover.
milestones.howTo: Have the weather mast switched on when a dust devil passes near the rover, more than {minDistance} m from the lander.
milestones.fact: On sol 215, Perseverance's microphone recorded the first sound of a dust devil on Mars as the whirlwind passed over the rover.
milestones.source: Murdoch et al., Nature Communications 13 (2022), 7505, "The sound of a Martian dust devil" (doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-35100-z)
